result.summary: This PR makes net_processing ignore MSG_WITNESS_TX entries in INV messages from wtxid-relay peers, since BIP-144 specifies that inv type is valid only in getdata, not announcements. It also reorders the disconnect check so that tx-relay-disabled peers are disconnected even for invalid inv types, and merges the seen_txids/seen_wtxids sets into one since only one type is ever used per message after the fix. A later revision preserves MSG_WITNESS_TX handling for peers without wtxid relay after evidence surfaced that the neutrino light client relies on it.
result.problem: Since wtxidrelay was introduced, the node has treated MSG_WITNESS_TX inv entries as valid txid announcements even though BIP-144 restricts that type to getdata messages, an oversight from the original implementation (PR #18044). This allows behavior BIP-144 forbids and complicates the announcement-handling code with two separate dedup sets.

resolved_concerns: darosior worried that dropping MSG_WITNESS_TX support for non-wtxid-relay peers could break an unmaintained codebase in the wild; author found evidence via 0xB10C that the neutrino light client does this, and revised the PR to keep allowing it for non-wtxid-relay peers, filing lightninglabs/neutrino#384 for the upstream issue.

result.card: This PR fixes net_processing to ignore MSG_WITNESS_TX entries received in INV announcements for wtxid-relay peers, correcting a BIP-144 non-compliance dating back to wtxidrelay's introduction (PR #18044). It also reorders the tx-relay disconnect check to fire even for invalid inv types, and merges two duplicate hash-dedup sets into one. During review, darosior raised a real compatibility concern that some peers (found by 0xB10C to include the neutrino light client) still send MSG_WITNESS_TX invs; the author revised the PR to preserve that behavior for non-wtxid-relay peers and filed an upstream issue with neutrino. The PR has concept ACKs from fjahr and l0rinc, no unresolved objections, and is ready for review as of the 2026-08-12 push. It has no stated dependencies and its impact is a narrow protocol-correctness fix rather than a major bug or feature.
